subject: Observability handoff: SIEM provisioning & tracing hooks for AcmeCo Private
messages:
From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@acmeco.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: AcmeCo SecOps <secops@acmeco.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability handoff for our Redwood Private deployment

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — we’re moving ahead with the Redwood Private deployment into our VPC and need to start the observability handoff so procurement / security can close the last few open items. Security has a short checklist but I wanted to align directly on a few technical constraints before we schedule the handoff call: 

- SIEM integration: we will ingest logs into Splunk (HEC) and need an approved HEC endpoint + token management model. Alternatively we may point to an on-prem Splunk forwarder in the DMZ.
- Network: our security team prefers egress to a small IP allowlist rather than general internet access. Can you provide the IP ranges and ports your private forwarder requires?
- Tracing hooks: we use OpenTelemetry across our services. We need to know whether Redwood can emit OTLP spans to our collector (OTLP/HTTP) or whether we must host an internal collector/forwarder.
- Data handling: retention defaults and redaction controls (PII, user identifiers) — what knobs do we have in the private build?

Can you send a short checklist of the items you need from us (certs, HEC token, network ACLs, S3 bucket, etc.) and ideally a small diagram showing where the forwarder will live (DMZ vs VPC). Procurement also asked for any SOC2 addenda or evidence artifacts we can attach to the PO.

Prefer a quick meeting this week if possible.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Shah
Head of SecOps, AcmeCo

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Observability handoff for our Redwood Private deployment

Hi Rajiv — thank you, this is exactly what we expected at this stage. I attached a short "Redwood Private Observability Checklist" (PDF) and a CSV with our published egress IPs; those should help your network team and procurement. Quick answers up front: 

- SIEM: We support two patterns: (1) direct Splunk HEC from the private forwarder (TLS + token), or (2) forwarder-in-DMZ that ships to your existing Splunk. If you prefer no outbound traffic from the VPC, option (2) is preferred.
- OTLP/Tracing: Redwood can emit OTLP/HTTP to your collector behind your ALB, or you can deploy the OpenTelemetry collector as a sidecar/forwarder in the DMZ which we will push traces to over mTLS.
- Data controls: retention is configurable per-customer; we support field-level redaction rules and can strip user-identifiers before export. For PCI/PHI we recommend our redact-and-audit flow (see checklist).

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Review attached checklist and fill the short columns we left for your team (HEC endpoint, token owner, preferred forwarder pattern).
2) Schedule a 45-min technical handoff (I’ll invite Stephanie + Vivek from our infra team).
3) We’ll provide SOC2 artifacts and a short architecture diagram for procurement.

I’ve attached: redwood-private-obsv-checklist.pdf and network-egress-ips.csv. Sending a calendar invite for Thu 4/5 10am PT — please let me know if that works.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[rachel_kim@redwood.ai]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Technical notes: ports, IP ranges, and OTEL config

Hi Rajiv — adding a few technical details ahead of the call so your network/security can validate the plan: 

1) Egress / firewall rules (recommended minimal set):
   - TCP 443 to Redwood egress IP ranges (see CSV) for S3/HTTPS endpoints and HEC if using direct to Redwood-managed HEC.
   - UDP/TCP 514 for Syslog if you plan to forward raw syslog (we primarily use structured JSON over TLS for logs).
   - TCP 8088 (optional) for direct Splunk HEC ingestion (if your Splunk is reachable from the forwarder).

2) IPs and clustering:
   - The CSV provides /24 ranges we use for dedicated pools; if you need fixed single-IP endpoints we can bake an NAT for Dedicated instances under a CIDR you provide.

3) TLS and auth model:
   - We support: bearer HEC tokens (rotateable) OR mutual TLS with client certs. For mTLS we expect a client cert with CN=acmeco-forwarder and subjectAltName include the forwarder hostname.

4) OTLP example (inline snippet):

   endpoint: https://otlp.acmeco.internal/v1/traces
   headers: {"Authorization": "Bearer <token>"}
   protocol: http/protobuf

   We will provide an otel-sample.yaml that your infra can drop in to a collector — it includes batching, retry, and resource attributes we recommend.

5) PII controls:
   - Redaction happens at the forwarder level: a user-configurable ruleset that can remove email, SSNs, or hashed user ids before logs are stored or exported. Audit logs for the redaction decisions are preserved for 90 days by default.

I attached the otel-sample.yaml to this thread. If we go with a DMZ forwarder, we will coordinate a handshake to exchange client certs and validate HEC tokens via a short mutual auth test.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: otel-sample.yaml (YAML)]

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@acmeco.com>

Subject: Re: Observability handoff for our Redwood Private deployment

Thanks Stephanie — that OTEL snippet is exactly what our infra team needed. A couple of clarifications from procurement/security before the handoff call:

- Procurement needs SOC2 Type II evidence or a short statement we can attach to the PO. Can you attach the SOC2 addendum and a concise flow diagram showing where logs/traces leave our environment (if at all)?
- We prefer no EGRESS to the public internet from our VPC. We will host a forwarder in the DMZ that speaks to your forwarder over mTLS. Is there any functionality lost with that pattern?
- For PIIs: we want to ensure that user-identifiers are redacted before any line items are forwarded to an external SaaS. Confirm the redact-and-audit flow will run in the forwarder.

If those are cleared we’re ready to sign off and move procurement forward. Can we stick to Thu 4/5 10am PT for the 45-min handoff?

Regards,
Rajiv
